heading: INT. UNDERWATER RESTAURANT - DINING ROOM - NIGHT

units.text: INT. UNDERWATER RESTAURANT - DINING ROOM - NIGHT
A glass-walled dining room sunk forty feet beneath a harbor.
Green water presses at the panes, and small silver fish dart past candlelit tables.
Every sound is muffled, like conversation in a cathedral.
A single table is occupied.
LEOPOLDINA "POLLY" ASHWORTH-DIAZ, sixty, in a velvet turban and enough pearls to flood the room, presides at the head of the table.
Her nephew CALVIN ASHWORTH, thirties, damp-palmed and rumpled, sits at her left.
At her right is her lawyer, ISADORA MCFEE, fifties, sharp as a letter opener, with a briefcase on her knees.
A WAITER hovers.
He is not a character; he is a rumor.
Calvin, darling, you've not touched your lobster.
units.name: POLLY

units.text: I'm not very hungry, Aunt Polly.
units.name: CALVIN

units.text: Nonsense. You've been hungry since the day you were born.
units.name: POLLY

units.text: Miss Ashworth-Diaz, shall we turn to the reason we're here?
units.name: ISADORA

units.text: Isadora, we are here for the lobster.
units.name: POLLY

units.text: We are here for the will.
units.name: ISADORA

units.text: We are here for both.
units.name: POLLY

units.text: Calvin looks at the water.
A fish stares back at him, then wheels away.
I've never liked being this far down.
units.name: CALVIN

units.text: That's the charm of it. Nobody can leave in a huff.
units.name: POLLY

units.text: You can leave in a rush, Calvin. There's a lift.
units.name: ISADORA

units.text: I'll stay.
units.name: CALVIN

units.text: Good boy.
units.name: POLLY

units.text: The waiter tops off Polly's wine.
She waves him off with two fingers and he vanishes behind a pillar.
Now. Here is how this will go. I have written a will. It names one heir. I will tell you the name over dessert.
units.name: POLLY

units.text: Over dessert?
units.name: CALVIN

units.text: The soufflé is divine.
units.name: POLLY

units.text: This is irregular.
units.name: ISADORA

units.text: So is my taste in nephews.
units.name: POLLY

units.text: Calvin lets out a nervous laugh and stops when nobody joins him.
He picks up his fork, studies the lobster, puts it down.
Aunt Polly, if it's me, I want you to know I'd be grateful.
units.name: CALVIN

units.text: And if it isn't?
units.name: POLLY

units.text: I'd still be grateful.
units.name: CALVIN

units.text: That is the first honest thing you've said in ten years.
units.name: POLLY

units.text: Miss Ashworth-Diaz, I really must insist.
units.name: ISADORA

units.text: Insist all you like, dear. The soufflé takes twenty minutes.
units.name: POLLY

units.text: Isadora opens her briefcase, withdraws a thick envelope, and sets it on the white tablecloth.
The candle gutters in the stillness.
I have here the sealed document. I am obliged to read it in the presence of the heir.
units.name: ISADORA

units.text: Then you are obliged to wait.
units.name: POLLY

units.text: Polly.
units.name: ISADORA

units.text: Isadora.
units.name: POLLY

units.text: They hold each other's eyes.
Calvin looks from one to the other, as a man might watch a tennis match from inside a fishbowl.
Above them, the harbor lights ripple.
A low groan comes from the hull.
The glass seems to flex.
A thin trickle of water runs down the west wall, and Polly's smile holds.
Is that supposed to happen?
units.name: CALVIN

units.text: The trickle? Oh, yes. It's decorative.
units.name: POLLY

units.text: It's not decorative.
units.name: ISADORA

units.text: Well, it is now.
units.name: POLLY

units.text: The trickle widens.
The candle flames lean.
Calvin half rises from his chair.
We should go.
units.name: CALVIN

units.text: Sit down, Calvin.
units.name: POLLY

units.text: Aunt Polly, the wall is leaking.
units.name: CALVIN

units.text: The wall is performing.
units.name: POLLY

units.text: This is absurd. Calvin, we are going.
units.name: ISADORA

units.text: Isadora, sit.
units.name: POLLY

units.text: Isadora doesn't sit.
A seam of glass cracks, a hair-thin line from floor to ceiling.
The sound is small and very precise.
Oh no.
units.name: CALVIN

units.text: Oh dear. Well. That is a new development.
units.name: POLLY

units.text: The line widens.
Water jets through it, flat and white.
The waiter's tray crashes somewhere out of sight.
Polly pushes back her chair, finally, and stands.
Calvin. The envelope.
units.name: POLLY

units.text: What about it?
units.name: CALVIN

units.text: Take it. Open it. Now.
units.name: POLLY

units.text: He seizes it, tears the flap, and pulls out a single sheet.
The water is at their ankles.
He reads, and his mouth falls open.
It says...
units.name: CALVIN

units.text: Read it aloud, darling.
units.name: POLLY

units.text: "To my nephew Calvin I leave nothing. To my lawyer, Isadora McFee, I leave everything, for she has been faithful."
units.name: CALVIN

units.text: Isadora stares at him.
Polly looks at Isadora with bright, fond eyes.
Well. Nobody ever tells you the plot twist will happen at forty feet.
units.name: POLLY

units.text: I didn't know.
units.name: ISADORA

units.text: Of course you didn't. That's what made it so lovely.
units.name: POLLY

units.text: The glass gives way.
The sea rushes in, and the candles go out one by one, and the last thing we see is Polly lifting her wine to the dark and saying, to nobody in particular:
Cheers.
units.name: POLLY
